caption: The drawing depicts a plan labeled "Sperry's Vauxhall Garden" at the top in bold brown lettering. The entire area is enclosed by a brown wooden fence. The background is a light, mottled green representing grass or ground. At the top, there are light brown and pinkish illustrations of flowering tree branches. Below, the garden is divided into sections with distinct green borders. There are six large square plots and one long rectangular plot, all with reddish-brown centers filled with evenly spaced dark green circles, representing planted beds or flower patches. On the right side of the layout, there are five large dark green circles in a vertical row, likely representing trees. Near the bottom center, there is a white rectangular structure with a faint diagonal roofline, possibly a greenhouse or pavilion. Two curved paths, depicted in dark beige, curve from a white arched gate at the bottom toward both the rectangular structure and a beige house with a red roof, four windows, and a central door at the bottom right corner. The drawing uses a pastel palette dominated by greens, browns, reds, and pinks, with all elements bordered by the brown fence and sitting on a textured light green background.
title: Sperry Gardens
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
